thread.title: Wamego Health Center receives national award for outstanding rural health organization

author: Sunflower State News
title: Wamego Health Center receives national award for outstanding rural health organization
text:
The National Rural Health Association announced on May 12 that Wamego Health Center has been named the recipient of the 2026 Outstanding Rural Health Organization award. The recognition is given to organizations that have made notable progress in advancing healthcare and improving lives in rural communities.
The award brings attention to Wamego Health Center’s commitment to serving Pottawatomie and Wabaunsee counties, as well as its transformation since its founding in 1916 into a modern facility known for clinical excellence.
A significant factor in the hospital’s success is its 25-year partnership with the City of Wamego and Ascension Via Christi. This collaboration combines local governance with access to Ascension Via Christi’s resources, technology, and expertise. The model has allowed the center to remain financially stable and expand services during a time when many rural hospitals face challenges nationwide.
“This award belongs to our dedicated physicians, providers and associates, many of whom are neighbors to the patients they serve,” said Brian Howells, Administrator of Wamego Health Center. “Receiving this national recognition is a credit to the strength of our partnership with the city and our commitment to ensuring high quality care remains accessible for the residents of Wamego and surrounding communities.”
In recent years, Wamego Health Center has increased its focus on outpatient services while maintaining critical access hospital status. New offerings include advanced wound care, infusion services, pain management, behavioral health programs, a swing bed program, and an active family practice clinic.
Wamego Health Center will be honored along with other recipients at NRHA’s 49th Annual Rural Health Conference in San Diego on May 21. “We’re extremely proud of this year’s winners,” said NRHA CEO Alan Morgan. “They have each made tremendous strides to advance rural health care, and we’re confident they will continue to help improve the lives of rural Americans.”
